name: Suno
product: AI music generator that turns text prompts or lyrics into full songs, with editing, stems and a studio for creators.
pricing_model: Freemium: 50 free credits/day; Pro about $10/month ($8 billed yearly), Premier about $30/month
lead_investors: Bond Capital (with IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet)
expansion_signal: Funds to go to scaling training infrastructure, growing product teams and speeding up global commercial rollout; CEO told Bloomberg headcount could grow up to 70% in 2026.
africa_use_case: Afrobeats, amapiano and gospel bedroom producers in Lagos, Accra, Johannesburg and Nairobi would pay $10/month to sketch beats, demos and jingles for clients, but today need a dollar card to subscribe.
notes: Low-priced monthly subscription with auto-renewal is a strong fit for Cozzipay's recurring billing. support@ and billing@suno.com are published on suno.com help pages (support, not partnerships). Ongoing copyright litigation with labels.

name: Higgsfield
hq_country: United States (San Francisco); engineering largely in Kazakhstan
product: AI video and image creation platform that bundles 35+ models for creators, marketers and studios.
pricing_model: Credit-based subscription; free tier, paid plans roughly $9-$19 to $129/month
round_amount_usd: Undisclosed extension (Series B was $400M in Aug 2026)
lead_investors: Extension: TCV and NVIDIA; Series B led by DST Global
expansion_signal: Says money will fund global infrastructure, hiring and commercial expansion into new markets; reports 40M+ users across 238 countries and territories.
africa_use_case: Nigerian and South African content agencies, Nollywood editors and TikTok/Instagram creators would pay for cheap ad videos and visuals, replacing costly shoots.
notes: Users already in 238 countries suggests African sign-ups exist but face card friction. Credits expire monthly; entry tiers are affordable. Series B ($400M at $5.4B, led by DST) announced 2026-08-17.

name: PixVerse
product: AI video generation app and web platform that creates cinematic clips from a prompt, photo or clip, now extending into real-time interactive worlds and games.
pricing_model: Freemium with daily credits; Standard about $10/month ($8 yearly); credit packs from $5
lead_investors: Not stated for extension; new investors include Alibaba, Lollapalooza Capital, Ivy Capital, Mirae Asset, BlueFocus
expansion_signal: Describes itself as a global platform with 150M+ users in 177+ countries; expanding into games, interactive livestreaming and entertainment.
africa_use_case: Young creators and meme pages in Nigeria, Kenya and Egypt would buy $5 credit packs or the $10 plan to make viral short videos for TikTok and Instagram.
founders: Changhu Wang (co-founder & CEO), Jaden Xie (co-founder & President)
notes: One-off $5 credit packs suit Cozzipay's one-click payments. Mass-market mobile product. Press contact listed in the release is Robyn Tan.

name: VideoGen
product: Browser-based AI video platform whose agents turn a brief or uploaded media into fully editable videos with AI voiceovers in 50+ languages.
pricing_model: Free plan; Pro $19/user/month, Advanced $39, Ultra $99 (billed yearly)
lead_investors: Not stated; round includes Y Combinator, Rebel Fund, Lobster Capital, Stretford End Capital
expansion_signal: Reports 5M+ users in more than 190 countries; one-click translation and 200+ voices in 50+ languages; funds to grow team and brand.
africa_use_case: Kenyan and Nigerian e-learning creators, SMEs and NGOs would pay $19/month to make training and product videos and translate them for local audiences without hiring editors.
notes: Small, bootstrapped-style team likely receptive to new payment rails. Also offers a Text-to-Video API.

name: each::labs
hq_country: United States (San Francisco); engineering in Istanbul, Türkiye
product: Generative media platform and API combining 600+ image, video and audio models with workflows, plus the each::studio workspace for creative teams.
pricing_model: Pay-as-you-go per model run; no seats or minimum spend
lead_investors: Revo Capital and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)
expansion_signal: Plans to build a sales and marketing team in San Francisco and expand each::studio for film and VFX teams; no country expansion named.
africa_use_case: African consumer-AI app builders and agencies in Lagos, Nairobi and Cairo could top up pay-as-you-go balances in local currency to power their own photo/video apps.
founders: Eftal Yurtseven (CEO), Ferhat Budak, Canberk Sinangil
notes: More developer/business-facing than consumer, but prepaid usage billing suits wallet top-ups. EBRD as co-lead may make emerging-market angles resonate. 750+ paying organisations.

name: Melius
product: Node-based AI creative canvas where an agent builds image, video and audio workflows to generate ad campaigns and creative assets from plain language.
pricing_model: Free plan; paid plans from $17/month (billed yearly), higher tiers $43 and $248
lead_investors: CRV (Series A); General Catalyst (seed)
expansion_signal: None stated beyond plans to grow the team, agents lab and sales operation.
africa_use_case: Small e-commerce brands and social-media managers in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg would pay $17/month to produce ad creatives for Meta and TikTok campaigns.
founders: Joowon Kim, Young Kim, Arnav Ramu (co-founders, ex-Ramp)
notes: Says it passed $1M annualized revenue within two months of leaving stealth in July 2026. Affordable entry tier.

name: Preview
product: AI video production workspace that combines scripting, storyboards, shot lists and multiple AI generation models for film teams.
pricing_model: Not found
lead_investors: Sequoia (per TheSaaSNews/Dealroom; a 36Kr report names HSG as lead)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Nollywood and Kenyan indie film crews and music-video directors could use it to storyboard and pre-visualise shoots cheaply before spending on production.
notes: Aimed at professional film teams; pricing unpublished, may be above typical African prosumer budgets. Lead investor reported inconsistently across sources.

name: Marker
product: AI-native word processor that helps writers ideate, draft, revise and collaborate without generating text for them.
pricing_model: Not found
lead_investors: Index Ventures (with LocalGlobe)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Substack/newsletter writers, journalists, novelists and students in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa would subscribe for a writing tool that keeps their own voice.
notes: Website marker.page per a tool directory listing. Pricing not yet public; early product.

name: Tolan (Portola)
product: AI companion app with a cartoon alien character that offers emotional support and helps users plan tasks, relationships and goals.
pricing_model: Tiered subscriptions: Lite about $11.99, Plus about $24.99, Unlimited about $199.99 (App Store listings)
lead_investors: Union Square Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Homebrew (lead not specified)
expansion_signal: Plans a free tier to widen access; 250,000+ monthly users.
africa_use_case: Busy working mothers and young professionals in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg would pay the Lite tier for a supportive companion that also organises errands and family plans.
founders: Quinten Farmer (CEO), Evan Goldschmidt, Ajay Mehta
notes: Revenue comes from memberships (ARR in double-digit millions). Reported as iPhone-only, a limit in Android-heavy African markets. Emotional-support AI carries safety/regulatory risk.

name: Wabi
product: Multiplayer personal AI agent and messenger that organises life into threads and builds mini-apps (trackers, polls, itineraries) inside chats.
pricing_model: Free for now; business model not yet set
lead_investors: IVP (with a16z, Forerunner, Amazon Alexa Fund)
expansion_signal: None stated; opened to all users on iOS, Android and Mac on 2026-10-19.
africa_use_case: Group-chat-heavy users in Nigeria and Kenya (friend groups, church and event committees) could use it to plan trips, contributions and events, paying for premium tiers once launched.
notes: Valued at $1.25B. No paid tier yet, so the pitch is about future paid plans. Available on Android, which helps in Africa.

name: Town
product: Personalised AI assistant ('Townie') that works across email, calendar, Slack, iOS and WhatsApp to triage inboxes, draft replies and run routines.
pricing_model: Free tier; Starter $15/month, Pro $49/month, Power $99/month; team plans per seat
lead_investors: Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures (Series A of $55M on 2026-06-03 led by Andreessen Horowitz)
expansion_signal: Series A post says it will broaden access beyond tech-savvy knowledge workers, citing users such as an international nonprofit director processing foreign-language requests.
africa_use_case: Small-business owners, consultants and accountants in Lagos and Nairobi who run their work through WhatsApp and Gmail would pay $15/month for an assistant that handles follow-ups.
notes: Already lives on WhatsApp, the dominant messaging app in Africa. Two rounds inside the window (Series A 2026-06-03, Series B 2026-10-19). Increasingly pitched at businesses.

name: Tomo
product: Personal AI companion you text, which tracks goals, budgets, fitness and habits, sends reminders and generates personalised mini-interfaces.
pricing_model: Subscription from about $19.99/month (third-party reviews)
lead_investors: Bain Capital Ventures (with Accel, Align Fund, Basis Set, Conviction, Pear VC)
expansion_signal: None stated; funds to grow team and expand the companion app.
africa_use_case: Ambitious students and young professionals in Accra, Lagos and Nairobi would pay for an accountability coach for savings goals, fitness and study routines.
founders: Justin Quan (co-founder & CEO), Raymond Chen (co-founder & CTO)
notes: Over 10,000 paying customers while in stealth. Primary interface is iMessage; Africa fit depends on WhatsApp/SMS support. $19.99 may be high for the market.

name: Pally
product: AI personal assistant you text over iMessage, RCS, WhatsApp or Telegram that manages inboxes, makes calls, books and checks out for you.
pricing_model: Free with near-unlimited usage; paid Cloud Mac add-on
lead_investors: Cyber Fund and Y Combinator (with Pioneer Fund, Founders Inc, 468 Capital)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: WhatsApp-first professionals and traders in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana could hand off replies, calls and bookings; paid add-ons could be bought via local-currency wallet.
founders: Haz Hubble, Wyatt Lansford (co-founders, per YC profile)
notes: Works natively in WhatsApp and Telegram, a strong Africa fit, but the core product is free, so revenue opportunity is limited to add-ons and future plans. Can complete purchases for users, which is a possible Cozzipay checkout integration.

name: Tab
product: Personal AI agent reached by texting a number on iMessage or WhatsApp that calls businesses, books and pays on your behalf after approval.
pricing_model: Not found
lead_investors: SV Angel, Valar Ventures, American Spirit (lead not specified)
expansion_signal: None stated; product still behind a waitlist and growing by word of mouth.
africa_use_case: Busy Lagos and Nairobi professionals who live in WhatsApp would pay for an agent that handles bookings and errand payments.
founders: Brennan Erbz, Stafford Schlitt, Ammar Amdani
notes: Agent that pays on users' behalf: Cozzipay could pitch both subscription billing and an agent-payment rail for African users. Amount raised undisclosed.

name: Fambot
product: AI 'chief of staff' for parents that reads school emails, calendars and WhatsApp groups and sends a daily text summary of tasks and decisions.
pricing_model: Free during beta; plans to charge roughly Netflix-level subscription
lead_investors: NextView Ventures and Baukunst (co-leads)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Middle-class parents in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg drowning in school WhatsApp groups would pay a few dollars a month for a daily digest of fees, events and deadlines.
founders: David Reich (CEO), Greg Karlin (CTO), Jason Morrow
notes: fambot.ai redirects to fambot.com. Paid plans not launched yet, so it is a good moment to get Cozzipay into the launch checkout. Available on iOS, Android and web.

name: Orbits
product: Bit, an AI household assistant (in-app and via text) that manages family calendars, lists and chores and books reservations, appointments and quotes.
pricing_model: Free during launch offer; subscriptions planned
lead_investors: a16z Speedrun (with N49P, Garage Capital)
expansion_signal: Funding to expand the consumer launch of Bit; no international markets named.
africa_use_case: Dual-income households in Nairobi, Lagos and Cape Town coordinating nannies, drivers, groceries and school runs would pay for a shared household assistant.
notes: Subscriptions not launched yet. Agent makes authorised purchases, a possible payment integration point. iOS and Android.

name: Onix
product: 'Personal Intelligence' app offering private AI guidance trained only on licensed knowledge from named health and wellness experts.
pricing_model: Not found
lead_investors: Alpha Edison (with Garage Capital, Ride Home Fund)
expansion_signal: Heading to full commercial availability later in 2026, with Android to follow iOS.
africa_use_case: Health-conscious urban professionals in South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria with limited access to specialists would pay for expert-backed wellness, sleep and nutrition guidance.
founders: David Bennahum (co-founder & CEO), Nicholas Nadeau (co-founder & CTO)
notes: Pre-commercial (iOS early access). Health-advice content may face regulatory scrutiny in some markets; experts are mostly US-based.

name: Ambi (Mistlabs)
hq_country: United States (San Francisco); offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen
product: Ambient AI assistant for iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch that can listen during meetings and the day to surface suggestions and start tasks in real time.
pricing_model: Not found (App Store lists a free download)
lead_investors: Luminous Ventures and Huaqin
expansion_signal: Hiring for go-to-market and speech-recognition engineering; dedicated hardware device planned.
africa_use_case: Consultants, lawyers and sales reps in Johannesburg, Lagos and Nairobi who live in back-to-back meetings would pay for live meeting notes and follow-ups.
notes: Apple-only for now, which narrows the African audience. Always-listening raises consent/privacy issues. ambi.ai redirects to ambi.ai/en.

name: Maple
product: Privacy-first AI chat app and desktop agent (Maple Work) running open models inside encrypted enclaves so the company cannot read user data.
pricing_model: Subscription: Pro $20/month; Max $100 and Max Plus $200/month
lead_investors: Epic Ventures (with Draper Associates, Planetary VC, Epoch VC)
expansion_signal: Already serves European customers through a partner-run EU server; targeting small businesses now and enterprise pilots next year; actively hiring.
africa_use_case: Lawyers, journalists, NGOs and fintech staff in Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa handling sensitive data under local data-protection laws would pay $20/month for private AI.
founders: Mark Suman (co-founder & CEO), Anthony Ronning (co-founder & CTO)
notes: Team of four; Bitcoin/privacy-oriented audience may value card-free payment. Reports 60x growth over three months.

name: Voyage Labs
product: Atlas, a personal AI travel agent in iMessage and on the web that plans, books and monitors flights, stays, dining and experiences.
pricing_model: Not found (private beta via waitlist)
lead_investors: Kleiner Perkins (with SignalFire, SV Angel)
expansion_signal: Funds to expand supplier partnerships across flights, stays, dining and experiences and to grow engineering.
africa_use_case: Frequent business and leisure travellers in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg would pay to plan and book trips; Cozzipay could also fund the bookings themselves.
founders: Manik Gupta (co-founder & CEO, ex-Uber CPO), Yogesh Jain (co-founder & CPTO)
notes: Agent books via supplier partnerships, so it handles large transaction values; a payment-method partnership could cover bookings as well as subscriptions. Pre-launch.

name: SuperMe
hq_country: United States (San Francisco); office in Ho Chi Minh City
product: Network of AI profiles built from real experts' knowledge; users ask a question and get a group chat of the best-matched expert AIs.
pricing_model: Free now; plans to cap questions and charge beyond the cap
lead_investors: Forerunner (Kirsten Green), with Greylock Partners
expansion_signal: Hiring to recruit experts in subject areas not yet covered; has an office in Vietnam.
africa_use_case: Early-stage founders and product managers in Lagos, Nairobi and Cape Town with little access to Silicon Valley mentors would pay for pitch-deck and growth advice.
notes: Paywall not yet live, so the pitch is to be the African payment option at monetisation. Also available inside ChatGPT/Claude via MCP.

name: Superpose
product: iOS AI camera app that suggests poses, gives real-time lighting and framing cues and turns one photo into several improved versions.
pricing_model: Freemium: 5 free generations/day; packs of 5 for $2.99 or 20 for $9.99
lead_investors: Khosla Ventures, Meitu, OVTR VC (lead not specified)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Image-conscious Gen Z users and Instagram/TikTok influencers in Lagos, Accra and Nairobi would buy $2.99 packs for better selfies and event photos.
notes: Small one-off purchases fit wallet payments well, but the app is iOS-only and sold through the App Store, where in-app billing rules limit alternative payments.

name: Scatter Lab (Zeta)
product: Zeta, an AI interactive story and character-chat app where users create characters and worlds and co-write stories by chatting.
pricing_model: Freemium (free chat; paid subscriptions)
lead_investors: Atinum Investment, SBVA, Mirae Asset Venture Investment (lead not specified)
expansion_signal: Strong growth in Japan; mobile app expanded globally in May 2026; company has said it is eyeing the US.
africa_use_case: Teen and twenty-something fans of K-drama, anime and webtoons in Nigeria, Kenya and Egypt would pay small subscriptions for immersive story chat.
notes: Very young user base; Zeta has introduced teen usage caps, so check content moderation and age-gating before pitching. Profitable (operating profit reported). Website also scatterlab.com.

name: Bunkerkids (WHIF / Wpp)
product: WHIF (Wpp), an AI interactive-story app where users build relationships with licensed webtoon/web-novel and original AI characters through chat.
pricing_model: Not found (paying users referenced)
lead_investors: Not specified; investors include Kolon Investment, Kakao Ventures, Mirae Asset Capital
expansion_signal: Operates in 13 countries with about 40% of sales from abroad; plans country-tailored content and a faster overseas push.
africa_use_case: Young women readers of romance web novels and webtoons in Nigeria, Ghana and South Africa would pay for interactive story chats with favourite characters.
notes: Strong localisation and international-revenue signal. Romance/BL focus: confirm content guidelines meet Cozzipay's brand-safety policy. App Store name is 'WHIF: Romance AI Chat'.

name: GasLab
product: Generative AI music app trained on licensed catalogues that attributes every generated track to contributing artists and shares revenue with them.
pricing_model: Subscription planned (not published; pre-launch guest list)
lead_investors: Not specified; angels include Eric Demuth (Bitpanda) and Bas Beerens (WeTransfer)
expansion_signal: Aims to become the leading global, fairly attributed genAI music platform.
africa_use_case: African producers and labels (amapiano, afro-house) could both license catalogues for royalties and pay to generate tracks, with local-currency payouts a natural add-on.
founders: Reinier Zonneveld, Cas Luuring, Thijs Emondts
notes: Pre-launch: good time to pitch checkout and artist payouts. Founder is a top-30 techno DJ with a global fan base.

name: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya
product: Music 'software label' releasing playful apps (e.g. bop, Stacks, Sampler) for remixing songs, stems and vocals without AI prompting.
pricing_model: Not found
lead_investors: Not specified; investors include Mantis VC, SV Angel, BoxGroup, Quiet Capital, Collaborative Fund
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Young music fans and TikTok creators in Lagos and Johannesburg would pay small amounts to remix popular tracks for social posts.
founders: Máuhan M. Zonoozy (founder, ex-Spotify head of innovation)
notes: Borderline for the segment: audio tools, not prompt-based AI. Business model unclear. Flagship app is iOS-only.

name: ArtMaster (Artie)
product: Artie, an AI piano teacher app that listens to you play and gives real-time feedback and step-by-step guided lessons.
pricing_model: Freemium; subscription about $35/month or $150/year in the US
lead_investors: Not specified; investors include Robert Kyncl, Jaroslav Beck, Moises, Nir Zicherman
expansion_signal: Coverage frames the company as targeting a global market of hundreds of millions of music learners; app listing covers seven languages.
africa_use_case: Church musicians, keyboard learners and parents of music students in Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya would pay for affordable piano lessons where private tutors are scarce.
notes: Annual plan (~$150, or $89.99 with voucher bought direct) is more viable than $35/month for Africa. Sells vouchers directly, outside the App Store, so an alternative payment method is feasible.

name: CHAOS
product: Music-creator collaboration app combining messaging, file sharing, live writing sessions and contribution tracking for attribution.
pricing_model: Not found (third-party listing: free download with in-app purchases)
lead_investors: Bridford Group (with Amuse)
expansion_signal: Funding supports expansion in the UK and US around its 29 October public launch.
africa_use_case: Producer-artist teams in Lagos, Accra and Johannesburg who collaborate across WhatsApp and Drive would pay for one workspace with clear credit splits.
notes: Sometimes branded 'Chaos AI', but AI is not the core of the product, so it is borderline for this segment. Very early stage.

name: Polar
product: AI-first browser for knowledge workers that runs agents on open tabs, schedules workflows and automates research, sales and ops tasks.
pricing_model: Free with daily credits; Individual from $20/month; Teams $50/seat/month
lead_investors: Madrona
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Freelance virtual assistants, recruiters and lead-gen agencies in Kenya, Nigeria and Egypt serving foreign clients would pay $20/month to automate prospecting and research.
notes: Clear self-serve subscription; Africa's large outsourced-work freelancer base is a natural user group. Legal entity reported as Recursive Intelligence, Inc.

name: Fish Audio
product: AI text-to-speech and voice-cloning platform with expressive voices and a large community voice library, plus an API.
pricing_model: Free plan; Plus about $11/month billed yearly ($15 monthly); Pro tier; pay-as-you-go API
lead_investors: Coreline Ventures and Capital Today
expansion_signal: None stated explicitly; reports 8M+ users of its open-source and hosted models.
africa_use_case: YouTube faceless-channel creators, audiobook narrators and ad agencies in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa would pay $11-15/month for voiceovers and cloned voices.
notes: Cheap creator plan with monthly auto-renew. Has faced creator complaints over voices uploaded without consent; check policy.

name: Whering
product: AI digital-wardrobe and styling app that lets users catalogue their clothes and get outfit suggestions from what they own.
pricing_model: Free; optional paid contribution for perks
lead_investors: eBay Ventures and Google AI Futures Fund
expansion_signal: Says it has passed 10M users globally; funds to expand AI wardrobe tools.
africa_use_case: Fashion-conscious young women and stylists in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg would pay for styling perks and resale/marketplace purchases.
notes: Monetisation is light (contributions plus marketplace), so Cozzipay's value is mostly marketplace checkout. Borderline for the segment (AI stylist/assistant). Emails published on whering.co.uk FAQ.

name: Zenzap
hq_country: Not found (staff in the US, Tel Aviv and Europe)
product: Mobile-first work messenger with AI agents, AI search, voice-note transcription and tasks, built to replace WhatsApp groups for frontline teams.
pricing_model: Free tier; paid from $51/month for up to 20 users; credit-based pricing for AI agents
lead_investors: Bessemer, Lightspeed, The Garage (lead not specified)
expansion_signal: Plans to hire in product and R&D; no new markets named.
africa_use_case: Restaurants, retail chains, logistics and construction SMEs in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa that coordinate staff over WhatsApp would pay $51/month for a compliant AI work chat.
founders: Guy Weiss, Noam Neumann, Jonatan Bien (co-founders)
notes: SMB tool more than consumer AI, so a stretch for this segment, but the WhatsApp-replacement pitch maps well to African workplaces. Clients listed are large US chains.
